query: For a high-entropy alloy initially designed as a single-phase solid solution, what testable mechanistic hypothesis explains whether and why it loses toughness or undergoes brittle fracture under mechanical loading in demanding engineering service? Define a controlled comparison that would reveal the governing behavior, predict observations relative to the initial baseline, identify the applicable service and loading boundaries, cite supporting prior evidence, and state a result that would falsify the hypothesis.

generation.hypothesis: In the equiatomic FCC Co-Cr-Fe-Mn-Ni high-entropy alloy (Cantor alloy), any significant decline in impact toughness or transition to brittle fracture after service exposure is governed by the stress-assisted nucleation and growth of Cr-rich σ (tetragonal DO22) precipitates along grain boundaries; these precipitates locally deplete Ni/Fe, raise grain-boundary cohesion energy mismatch, and block dislocation glide, so that under high triaxial stress states the alloy fractures by intergranular cleavage rather than the normal ductile transgranular mode.
generation.material_initial_state: Solution-annealed, single-phase FCC CoCrFeMnNi alloy (average grain size 20–30 µm, no detectable second phases, CVN impact energy ≈ 250 J at −196 °C).
generation.intervention: Thermal ageing at 500 °C for 1000 h in air followed by high-triaxiality mechanical loading (e.g., sharp-notch tensile or Charpy V-notch impact) at −196 °C.
generation.conditions: Ageing temperature 500 ± 10 °C; cryogenic test temperature −196 ± 5 °C; stress triaxiality ≥ 0.7; strain rate 10²–10³ s⁻¹ (Charpy) or 10⁻³ s⁻¹ (quasi-static).
generation.structural_mediator: Continuous or semi-continuous chains of σ-phase precipitates (20–200 nm) decorating prior-austenite grain boundaries and triple junctions, with adjacent Ni/Fe-depleted zones (~50 nm wide).
generation.mechanism: 1) Ageing induces σ-phase precipitation at high-energy boundaries driven by Cr segregation; 2) these particles introduce coherency strains and Ni/Fe depletion that reduce boundary cohesive strength; 3) during cryogenic loading, reduced dislocation activity and high triaxial stress localise plasticity along these weakened boundaries; 4) cracks nucleate and propagate intergranularly, producing brittle fracture and lower impact toughness.
generation.predicted_outcome: Relative to the unaged baseline, the aged alloy will show (a) ≥ 60 % drop in Charpy impact energy, (b) transition from ductile dimples to predominantly intergranular cleavage facets on fracture surfaces, (c) TEM/EDS confirmation of σ-phase and Ni/Fe depletion at boundaries, and (d) negligible change in room-temperature hardness (solid solution strengthening unchanged).
generation.baseline: As-solution-annealed alloy exhibiting high cryogenic toughness (CVN ≈ 250 J, > 50 % ductility) with fully ductile dimpled fracture morphology and no detectable σ-phase.
generation.boundary: Applies when: (i) cumulative 400–600 °C exposure exceeds ~500 h; (ii) Cr content ≥ 20 at % and grain boundaries not stabilised by B-elements; (iii) service temperature ≤ −100 °C and loading induces stress triaxiality ≥ 0.7. Outside these ranges (e.g., no prolonged 500 °C exposure, or service > 0 °C) σ-phase remains absent or plasticity suppresses boundary fracture, so toughness is retained.
generation.uncertainty: Moderate: kinetics of σ-phase precipitation in multicomponent HEAs is still being quantified; the critical particle fraction for embrittlement and precise impact-energy drop may vary with grain size and prior cold work.

falsification_experiment.design: Prepare two specimen sets from identical solution-annealed CoCrFeMnNi plates: (1) as-received baseline; (2) aged 500 °C/1000 h. Perform (a) Charpy V-notch tests at −196 °C and +25 °C, (b) notched tensile tests (stress triaxiality ~0.8) at −196 °C, and (c) TEM/EDS on fracture-surface extraction replicas and site-specific FIB lift-outs from grain boundaries.
measurements: Fracture surface mode fraction (ductile vs intergranular) by SEM
Presence, size and chemistry of σ-phase at grain boundaries via TEM/EDS
Notched tensile fracture strain and stress
Room-temperature Vickers hardness to gauge matrix strength
falsification_experiment.falsification_rule: If the aged specimens retain ≥ 80 % of baseline cryogenic Charpy energy AND fracture surfaces remain > 80 % ductile transgranular with no detectable σ-phase at boundaries (≤ 1 vol %), the hypothesis is falsified.
